question.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}xyz\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{4-2z},\,0\le y\le x\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}xyz\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{\int }_{0}^{x}xyz\,dy\,dx\,dz.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{\int }_{0}^{x}xyz\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}xyz\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}xz{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}xz(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\,dx\,dz \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{x}^{3}z\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{x}^{3}z\,dx\,dz & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2z}}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-2z}}\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{4}(4-2z)^{2}z\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4z-4{z}^{2}+{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4z-4{z}^{2}+{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z & =\frac{1}{2}{[2{z}^{2}-\frac{4}{3}{z}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(8-\frac{32}{3}+4)-0 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
